Each mutant removes one guarantee and must redden exactly the axes in `expect` (pairwise distinct within the spec). `red_re` anchors on the jest failure header `● <suite> › <axis> ` (ITRV §A44/§A104). Anchors are CODE lines only — the fix's comments may be reworded freely. `tree`/`subject` are placeholders — run the matrix on a copy with the paths substituted (§A145). Subject: AggregateExecutor — MIN / MAX of a group with no values, and the absent aggregate in the result row. Anchors are code lines of the shipped fix (ems__Bug 37c80e59, PR #4580): rewriting one of them means moving its anchor and re-taking every `expect` from a finished driver run — pairwise-distinct sets stay required.

M7_max_empty_literal._note: MAX of no values builds Literal("") again — it throws "Literal value cannot be empty" and fails the query.

M7b_unbound_aggregate_kept_in_row._note: An unbound aggregate is written into the row as undefined: the variable reads as bound and toJSON() throws in the CLI output. DEFENSIVE (ITRV §A35/§A135): the group row always reaches the output through Project, which drops an undefined value (`executeProject`: `if (value !== undefined)`) — so no axis can redden; the guard keeps the raw group row honest for any future consumer (has() / toJSON()).

M16_empty_input_min_max_sample_literal._note: MIN / MAX / SAMPLE over an EMPTY input with GROUP BY build Literal("") again — "Literal value cannot be empty" fails the whole query.
